page: Microsoft Azure E20as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, it supplies 20 vCPUs mapped to 10 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Local ephemeral storage includes a 344 GB solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are absent.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate robust memory subsystem efficiency alongside balanced computation. The platform achieves strong tier results in PassMark memory testing (2895.15) and stress-ng single-core execution (2707.78). Multi-core operations register in the middle performance bracket across stress-ng (27048.94) and Geekbench multi-core (11290.0). Memory throughput scales up to 86.09 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 47.83 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a Redis SET throughput of 20.16 million operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs center around computation-heavy acceleration. While cryptographic acceleration is aided by AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction flags, the CPU lacks AVX-512 extensions and dedicated matrix accelerators. Consequently, large language model generation drops significantly on medium models (6.79 tokens/sec) and prompt processing registers weakly on 70B models (3.53 tokens/sec). Resource density provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for high-RAM services, although CPU-bound vector scaling is constrained.

The configuration serves workloads characterized by elevated RAM capacity demands and steady I/O throughput. Representative deployments include in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, static web serving clusters, and enterprise enterprise-tier data processing workflows that operate independently of specialized hardware accelerators.
